record.paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
record.context_brief: Upper bound for minimal neighbour-finding trees in degeneracy graphs
record.original_question: Let x⁰ be a degenerate vertex of a bounded polytope X, let G⁰₊ be the positive degeneracy graph whose nodes are the bases associated with x⁰, let U be the number of such bases, and let σ be the degeneracy degree of x⁰. Among the trees in G⁰₊ that connect x⁰ to all neighbouring vertices of x⁰, a minimal tree is one with the smallest possible number of nodes. Is ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋ always an upper bound on the number of nodes needed for such a minimal tree?

evidence.quote: This might lead to the determination of a so called minimal tree Gmin -o (a tree with minimal number of nodes). We conjectured that the greatest
integer smaller or equal to U/(tr+ 1) is an upper bound on the number of nodes needed to form a minimal tree.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X ⊂ ℝⁿ be a bounded polytope defined by a system of linear inequalities/equalities, and let x⁰ be a degenerate vertex of X (i.e., a vertex associated with more than one feasible basis). Let U denote the number of feasible bases associated with x⁰, and let σ be the degeneracy degree of x⁰ (the number of "extra" basic variables at x⁰ beyond a non-degenerate basis, so that U bases sit at x⁰).

Define the positive degeneracy graph G⁰₊ to be the graph whose node set is the collection of these U bases at x⁰, with two bases joined by an edge whenever they differ by a single pivot step using a positive pivot rule (so that each edge corresponds to a feasible simplex pivot between two bases at x⁰). 

A "neighbour-finding tree" rooted at x⁰ is a subtree of G⁰₊ that, by means of pivots leaving the bases of its nodes, reaches every vertex of X adjacent to x⁰ (i.e., every neighbouring vertex of x⁰ in the 1-skeleton of X). A minimal neighbour-finding tree is one with the smallest possible number of nodes.

Question: Is it true that for every degenerate vertex x⁰ of every bounded polytope X, the number of nodes of a minimal neighbour-finding tree is at most ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on degeneracy graphs and minimal neighbour-finding (N-) trees return general references to the theory of degeneracy graphs and the neighbourhood problem (e.g., survey chapters in Springer volumes and ORiON), but none of the readily available sources explicitly confirm or refute the conjectured upper bound ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋ on the number of nodes of a minimal N-tree. The status of the conjecture could not be verified from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Degeneracy problems in mathematical programming and degeneracy graphs (ORiON)
status_evidence.snippet: The neighbourhood problem is solved by a new approach to determine a minimal N-tree (N for neighbour), and an efficient method to determine all vertices of a convex polytope is described.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the framework of minimal N-trees in degeneracy graphs but does not state the ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋ bound.

status_evidence.title: Degeneracy Graphs (Springer chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Chapter on degeneracy graphs developing the theory of bases at degenerate vertices.
status_evidence.claim: General reference; does not directly resolve the conjectured bound.
